title: Record of meeting Summary of Discussions Among Members of the Community Depository Institutions Advisory Council April 11, 2024
summary: CDIAC council members reported the economy remains surprisingly resilient despite persistent inflationary pressures driven by strong consumer demand, with a bifurcation between upper- and lower-income groups. Inflation has moderated from peak levels but remains stubbornly high, with services inflation persisting due to labor costs while goods inflation slows. The council expressed cautious optimism regarding the economic outlook.
key_points: Economy is resilient but faces persistent inflation challenges, with lower-income households experiencing greater difficulty keeping up with rising prices
Inflation has moderated from peak but remains stubbornly high; services inflation persists due to labor costs while goods inflation is slowing
Council members expressed doubts about near-term feasibility of the 2% inflation target in the current environment
Housing prices remain restrictive for most consumers despite moderation in price increases; some areas seeing influx of out-of-state buyers placing additional supply pressure
Labor markets remain tight for non-skilled and blue-collar workers especially in manufacturing and trade sectors; immigration helping to fill gaps
Labor costs have moderated from 6-7% pay increases last year to approximately 4-5% this year
Insurance costs have risen significantly and technology costs are up as much as 10% year-over-year in 2024
why_it_matters: The CDIAC meeting provides real-economy feedback from depository institutions on economic conditions and inflation dynamics. Council members' observations about inflation remaining stubbornly high, the bifurcation between income groups, and doubts about near-term 2% inflation target achievement are relevant signals for Fed policy. The moderation in labor cost growth from 6-7% to 4-5% is a notable data point for assessing whether wage pressures are easing.
macro_context: Council members described a bifurcated economy with upper-income groups faring better than lower-income groups. Inflation is hurting low- and moderate-income families most, with increased food assistance requests. Labor costs are moderating but remain elevated. Services inflation persists while goods inflation is moderating. Housing affordability remains a challenge. The council expressed cautious optimism given stable consumer confidence and slow return of small business capital investment.
market_structure_context: CDIAC members noted depository institutions are facing rising technology costs (up to 10% year-over-year versus prior 2-3% averages) and constrained insurance availability. Banks are offering higher hourly rates for entry-level positions like tellers, but are benefiting from talent pool expansion as large banks and tech firms shed jobs. These dynamics affect operating costs and competitive positioning for community depository institutions.
important_numbers: 2% inflation target (referred to as unlikely to achieve near-term)
